samples.summary: Paste of a large clipboard payload now goes through spread-based `rangeOf`, which throws RangeError on big grids (unbounded untrusted input → client-side DoS / post-commit abort)
samples.evidence: This delta deletes the loop-based `gridRange()` (which scanned `grid.keys()` with a plain for-of and was safe for any grid size) and replaces both call sites with `rangeOf()` from packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:18-27, which computes `Math.min(...rows)` / `Math.max(...cols)` by spreading one argument per cell. Attack/abuse vector: the grid is built straight from attacker- or user-controlled clipboard data with no size cap — `string2grid(target, text)` (grids.ts:113) creates one entry per TSV field, and `html2grid` (grids.ts:164) one per `<td>`. A clipboard payload of roughly >100k cells (e.g. 2,500 rows × 50 cols, or a single crafted `text/plain` blob from a malicious page that called `navigator.clipboard.write`) makes the spread exceed V8's argument limit and throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. At sheet.ts:2255 that throw aborts the paste before any write and is swallowed by the view's `catch` (spreadsheet.ts:722, worksheet.ts:4905), so the user just gets a silently dead paste. Worse, the second call site — `selectPastedRange` → `rangeOf(grid)` at sheet.ts:2389 — runs AFTER `store.endBatch()` has committed, so for a large internal copy/cut the data is already written but the exception escapes `paste()`, meaning `paste` never returns, `clearCopyBuffer()` (spreadsheet.ts:718 / worksheet.ts:4902) never runs and `render()` is skipped, leaving the view stale and the copy buffer state inconsistent with the committed store. Note the codebase already treats unbounded bulk input as a hazard elsewhere: CSV import enforces MAX_IMPORT_CELLS=40_000 and MAX_IMPORT_BYTES (import/csv-importer.ts:91,155); the paste path has no equivalent bound.

samples.summary: `paste()` applies clipboard content with no cell-count or byte cap, unlike CSV import which enforces MAX_IMPORT_CELLS/MAX_IMPORT_BYTES
samples.evidence: `Sheet.paste` (sheet.ts:2169) converts the whole clipboard payload into a grid (`string2grid`, `html2grid`) and writes it via `setGrid` inside one batch with no upper bound on rows/cols/bytes. A hostile page that populates the clipboard (or a user copying a huge external table) can drive an arbitrarily large synchronous parse + store batch, freezing the tab. The same package deliberately bounds this exact class of input for file import (packages/sheets/src/import/csv-importer.ts:91 `MAX_IMPORT_BYTES = 8_000_000`, :155 `MAX_IMPORT_CELLS = 40_000`), so the paste path is an unguarded parallel entry point for the same untrusted data. This delta makes the gap sharper because the newly-used `rangeOf` fails hard rather than degrading at large sizes.
searchedFor: grep for 'paste(' call sites in packages/sheets/src and packages/frontend/src

verdict.reason: The described code IS present: rangeOf at coordinates.ts:18-27 spreads one argument per grid cell (Math.min(...rows)); it is called at sheet.ts:2255 (pre-commit) and at sheet.ts:2389 via selectPastedRange, which indeed runs after store.endBatch() in the finally at sheet.ts:2376; the throw would be swallowed by the view catches at spreadsheet.ts:722 and worksheet.ts:4905; and string2grid (grids.ts:113-126) / html2grid (grids.ts:164-179) apply no size cap. So this is neither not-present nor already-guarded, and the mechanical defect is real. It is refuted as OUT-OF-SCOPE for the Security lens. The grid is built solely from the user's own clipboard, read under the user's own paste gesture in their own browser (spreadsheet.ts:689-713, worksheet.ts:4872-4897), so no trust boundary is crossed: no authorization surface is weakened (the read-only gate at spreadsheet.ts:690 still holds, and a throw at sheet.ts:2255 fails closed before any write), and there is no secret, injection sink, signature/HMAC check, SSRF, deserialization, or path handling involved. Blast radius is confined to the pasting user's own session - a dead paste, or a stale view with an inconsistent local copy buffer - with no cross-user or cross-tenant effect and no amplification: Array.from(grid.keys()) already materializes the same N, and a successful paste of that N would perform N store writes anyway, so the spread is not a resource-exhaustion multiplier, it merely throws. The claimed attacker payoff (a malicious page calling navigator.clipboard.write) amounts to making the victim's next paste into their own sheet silently fail - an availability annoyance in the victim's own client, not a security-boundary violation. That makes it a robustness/correctness defect, explicitly deferred by this lens's "NOT your lane - general logic bugs (correctness lens)" rule; it is already carried against the same line in the correctness lane (.agent-review/correctness/summary.md:5 records coordinates.ts:24 rangeOf spread / stack overflow on large pastes as confirmed), so dropping it from the security gate does not lose the issue. Refuted on lane fit only, not on facts - the bug is real and should be fixed.
